name: DeepLabCut
description: Markerless 2D/3D pose estimation
details: Python-based toolkit for markerless pose estimation that learns to locate user-defined body parts in video from a small set of hand-labeled frames. It outputs per-frame keypoint coordinates with confidence scores, supports 2D and multi-camera 3D tracking, and is widely used across species and lab setups as an upstream input for behavior classifiers.

name: SLEAP
description: Multi-animal pose estimation
details: Deep-learning system for tracking the poses of multiple animals at once in video. It bundles a graphical interface for labeling frames, training models and running inference, with a choice of many network architectures plus several strategies for grouping body parts and maintaining identities. Tested on flies, bees, mice and gerbils, it is fast enough for real-time closed-loop experiments and outputs keypoint tracks per individual.

name: DeepPoseKit
description: Pose estimation toolkit
details: Software toolkit for estimating animal body-part locations directly from images or video using deep learning. It uses an efficient multi-scale network with GPU-based peak detection to place keypoints at subpixel precision, aiming for faster processing without losing accuracy. It has been applied to both laboratory and field footage, including groups of interacting animals.

name: Lightning Pose
description: Semi-supervised, multi-view pose estimation
details: Open-source pose estimation package that uses semi-supervised learning to make use of unlabeled video alongside labeled frames, and supports multi-view setups. Its approach includes Bayesian ensembling of model predictions and cloud-friendly tooling, and it is aimed at producing smoother, more reliable keypoint tracks across species.

name: Facemap
description: Mouse orofacial tracking and neural prediction
details: Framework for tracking orofacial movements in head-fixed mice and relating them to neural activity. A keypoint tracker follows facial features such as the mouth, nose and whiskers from video and can be adapted to a new lab with only a handful of labeled frames; the keypoints can then feed a neural network that predicts large-scale recorded neural activity. Its speed also makes it usable for real-time experiments.

name: OpenPose
description: Real-time multi-person 2D keypoint detection
details: Real-time system for detecting 2D keypoints of multiple people in images and video, covering body, foot, hand and facial landmarks. It works bottom-up, first finding body parts and then linking them into individuals, so speed stays stable as the number of people grows. It was built for human pose rather than animals.

name: MMPose
description: General-purpose pose estimation toolbox (OpenMMLab)
details: General-purpose, open-source pose estimation toolbox from the OpenMMLab project, built on PyTorch. It provides a large collection of model architectures and pretrained weights for 2D keypoint detection in humans, animals and other targets, and is mainly suited to users comfortable configuring and training deep-learning models in Python.

name: YOLO (Ultralytics)
description: Real-time keypoint/pose estimation; also object detection and segmentation
details: Python package providing YOLO models for real-time object detection, instance segmentation and keypoint (pose) estimation. Users can train custom models on their own labeled images or video frames to detect animals and their body parts, producing bounding boxes, masks and keypoint coordinates; it is often used as a fast front end for downstream behavior analysis.

name: SuperAnimal / DLC Model Zoo
description: Pretrained cross-species DeepLabCut models, usable without new labelling
details: Collection of pretrained pose estimation models distributed with DeepLabCut that work across many species, including top-view mice and quadrupeds, without requiring new manual labels. The models can be run directly on video or fine-tuned on a small amount of lab-specific data, and include tooling for video adaptation to reduce frame-to-frame jitter.

name: APT (Animal Part Tracker)
description: Multi-animal body-part tracking with a labelling GUI; exports .trk (Branson lab)
details: Pose tracking software from the Branson lab that combines a graphical labeling interface with deep-learning model training and inference. It tracks body parts of single or multiple animals in video and exports the resulting trajectories as .trk files.

name: DeepGraphPose
description: Pose estimation using graph-based spatiotemporal priors
details: Pose estimation method that adds spatial and temporal constraints on top of a deep network, exploiting the fact that body parts keep plausible distances from each other and move smoothly between frames. Because it learns from both labeled and unlabeled frames, it needs fewer hand-labeled examples and produces more robust keypoint tracks, which can improve downstream behavior segmentation.

name: STPoseNet
description: Spatiotemporal network for real-time, occlusion-robust mouse pose estimation
details: YOLOv8-based keypoint detector for mouse behavior videos that adds temporal tracking to cope with occlusion and motion blur. It uses the previous frame's detections to guide the next frame and a Kalman filter to estimate missing keypoints, aiming for real-time and more stable pose tracks in standard mouse assays.

name: KineWheel-DeepLabCut
description: Automated paw labelling for DeepLabCut training using alternating UV and white-light stroboscopy
details: Hardware and software setup that automatically generates training labels for paw tracking with DeepLabCut. Fluorescent paw markers become visible under alternating UV and white-light strobe illumination, so paw positions found in UV frames can be transferred to the adjacent white-light frames used for training. It was demonstrated on a harness-fixed mouse running on a transparent wheel with a mirror.

name: DeepFly3D
description: 3D pose estimation for tethered Drosophila
details: Software for estimating the 3D pose of tethered adult Drosophila from multiple synchronized camera views, and adaptable to other animals. It does not require manual camera calibration, automatically detects and corrects pose errors, and uses active learning to improve over time. The resulting 3D joint angles can be used for behavioral embedding and kinematic analysis.

name: Anipose
description: 3D pose estimation from synchronized cameras
details: Open-source toolkit that turns 2D DeepLabCut tracking from multiple synchronized cameras into 3D pose. It includes camera calibration, filtering of 2D tracking errors, triangulation with temporal and spatial smoothing, and a pipeline for batch-processing many videos. It has been used with mice, flies and humans.

name: DANNCE
description: 3D landmark detection from multi-view video
details: Deep-learning tool that estimates 3D landmark positions on freely moving animals from multi-camera video. Rather than triangulating separate 2D predictions, it reasons over the combined multi-view information to produce 3D keypoints, and is mainly used for rodents in arenas recorded by several calibrated cameras.

name: OpenMonkeyStudio
description: Markerless 3D pose estimation for freely moving macaques
details: Markerless motion capture system for estimating 3D pose of freely moving rhesus macaques in a large enclosure surrounded by many machine-vision cameras. The multi-view recordings are used to train a view-invariant network that infers pose automatically during unconstrained movement, supporting action recognition and analysis of social interactions.

name: JARVIS
description: Multi-camera 3D markerless motion capture: calibration, 3D annotation, training and inference
details: Markerless motion capture toolbox for 3D pose estimation from multiple synchronized cameras. It covers the full workflow, including camera calibration, annotation of keypoints in 3D across views, network training and inference, and outputs 3D keypoint trajectories of the tracked animal.

name: 3DTracker-FAB
description: 3D video-based markerless tracking of interacting rodents with depth cameras
details: Markerless 3D tracking system for interacting rodents that combines several depth cameras to reconstruct the scene in 3D. Skeleton models are fit to the reconstructed animals to estimate body-part positions, which are then used to recognize social and sexual behaviors. It can follow two rats even when they overlap, such as during mounting.

name: TRex
description: Real-time, identity-preserving tracking
details: Tracking software for large groups of animals in video that uses background subtraction and can run in real time, including closed-loop experiments. Beyond positions it estimates outlines, head and rear orientation and visual fields, and offers deep-learning-based identification of unmarked individuals to keep identities consistent. It comes with a cross-platform graphical interface for exploring the results.

name: idtracker.ai
description: Markerless identity tracking for animal groups
details: Deep-learning software that tracks groups of unmarked animals in video while keeping each individual's identity consistent over time. It outputs per-animal trajectories and is commonly used for collectives such as fish, flies and mice recorded in a lab arena.

name: AlphaTracker
description: Multi-animal tracking, pose, and behavioral clustering
details: Pipeline for tracking multiple unmarked mice that pairs top-down pose estimation with unsupervised clustering to discover behavioral motifs. It has modest hardware requirements, can be run through graphical interfaces or the command line, and outputs identity-tracked keypoints plus behavior clusters for studying individual and social behavior.

name: Tracktor
description: OpenCV-based single- and multi-object tracker
details: Image-based tracking software built on OpenCV that follows a single animal in noisy conditions or multiple animals in uniform backgrounds while preserving identities. Users set tracking parameters in a designated spot without writing code, and it produces trajectories along with summary metrics such as distance, speed, activity, time in zones and distance to neighbors.

name: ToxTrac
description: Fast tracker for one or several animals
details: Fast image-based tracking program for one or several animals across multiple arenas in lab video, applicable to insects, fish, rodents and other species. It requires no prior knowledge of body shape, includes camera calibration and distortion correction, preserves individual identities, and exports locomotion statistics and heat maps in real-world units.

name: ezTrack
description: Blob-based location and freezing tracking
details: Set of interactive Python notebooks for video tracking that are designed for researchers without programming experience. One module tracks the location of a single animal across many kinds of tasks and another scores freezing behavior. It supports batch processing, regions of interest, cropping out tethers or cables, and produces frame-by-frame output that aligns easily with neural recordings.

name: LiveMouseTracker
description: Long-term mouse tracking via RFID and depth cameras
details: Open-source system for long-term monitoring of groups of mice in a home-cage-like arena, combining a depth camera with RFID identification. RFID keeps individual identities over days, while the depth video is used to extract positions and detect social and individual behavior events.

name: TrackMate
description: ImageJ/Fiji object-tracking plugin
details: Fiji/ImageJ plugin for detecting and tracking objects in 2D and 3D image sequences. Newer versions integrate machine-learning and deep-learning segmentation into the tracking pipeline. It is primarily designed for bioimaging such as microscopy of cells and particles, rather than for whole-animal behavior video.

name: C-Trax
description: Tracking of walking flies in groups
details: Open-source software for tracking groups of walking fruit flies in video while maintaining individual identities. It produces per-fly trajectories that can be used for downstream behavior analysis.

name: AnimalTA
description: GUI tracking of multiple animals across varied setups
details: Tracking program with a graphical interface meant to be usable without coding or image-analysis expertise. It handles many videos and multiple arenas, copes with low-quality footage and heterogeneous backgrounds, and includes tools to correct camera shake, lighting changes and perspective distortion as well as to fix tracking errors. It then computes trajectory measures such as speed, distance, latency to areas and contacts between individuals.

name: BioTracker
description: Modular video-tracking framework
details: Open-source computer vision framework for building animal tracking software. It provides the core components such as video input/output, overlays and user interaction, includes several tracking algorithms for different recording conditions, and is mainly intended for programmers who want to add their own problem-specific tracking modules.

name: FlyTracker
description: Tracking and feature extraction for interacting flies
details: Software for tracking interacting fruit flies in video and extracting behavioral features from their trajectories, such as positions, orientations and body-part measures, which can be used for downstream behavior classification.

name: FicTrac
description: Spherical-treadmill path tracking for tethered insects
details: Tool for reconstructing the fictive path of a tethered animal walking on a spherical treadmill by tracking the rotation of the ball from video. It is commonly used with insects in virtual-reality and closed-loop experiments.

name: ZebraZoom
description: Zebrafish larva and adult behaviour tracking
details: Program for tracking zebrafish larvae and adults in video and detecting their discrete movement bouts. It extracts large-scale statistics on locomotor patterns and can use supervised machine learning to classify larval movements into maneuver types such as forward swims, turns and escapes, making it suited to high-throughput screens.

name: Stytra
description: Zebrafish tracking with closed-loop stimulus control
details: Python package for larval zebrafish behavioral experiments that combines timed stimulus presentation with real-time tracking of position, orientation, tail and eye movements. It works for both freely swimming and head-restrained fish, supports closed-loop stimulation, interfaces with external devices such as imaging setups, and logs data and metadata in standardized formats.

name: OCTRON
description: Segment-Anything-based segmentation and tracking in a napari GUI
details: Pipeline for multi-animal segmentation, detection and tracking run through a napari graphical interface. It uses large segmentation foundation models to speed up mask annotation, then trains compact task-specific models for full-body shape or fast centroid tracking, with an interactive tool for curating tracks. It suits animals with deformable bodies where sparse keypoints are not enough.

name: FastTrack
description: Fast 2D tracking of multiple objects, with manual correction
details: Cross-platform software for fast 2D tracking of many deformable objects, including animals and cells, in video. It can handle a changing number of objects, includes automatic tuning of tracking parameters, and provides a manual correction interface for fixing identity swaps.

name: Tierpsy Tracker
description: Multi-worm tracking and phenotyping for C. elegans
details: Open-source software for tracking multiple C. elegans worms in video and extracting detailed posture and locomotion features for behavioral phenotyping.

name: Argos
description: Tracking multiple animals in cluttered or visually complex environments
details: Toolkit for tracking multiple unmarked animals in visually complex environments with uneven lighting, where simpler trackers struggle. It includes tools to compress video based on movement, build training sets for a neural-network animal detector, track multiple animals over long recordings, and review and correct tracks through simple graphical interfaces.

name: Markerless Mouse Tracking (MaSoMoTr)
description: Identity-preserving tracking of interacting mice for social experiments
details: Markerless tool for tracking two identical-looking mice interacting in a cage, built to minimize identity switches during social experiments. It combines classical tracking with deep learning, is trained on a small number of annotated images, and outputs body masks plus snout and tail-base coordinates for each mouse. It works with bedding and with fiber-optic or headstage implants.

name: PyMouseTracks
description: Raspberry Pi video plus RFID tracking of multiple mice
details: Low-cost system combining Raspberry Pi video recording with RFID identification to track several mice in a user-defined arena or home cage, from minutes to days. Acquisition runs on the Pi and analysis is done offline, producing identity-tagged trajectories; output can be passed to DeepLabCut for pose estimation and to Traja for trajectory analysis.

name: CaT-z
description: 3D tracking and automated behaviour classification from RGB-D depth cameras
details: Uses low-cost RGB-D depth cameras to segment, track and classify the behavior of individual rats in three dimensions. It follows five anatomical landmarks and recognizes seven behaviors, and because it relies on depth rather than color it works in the dark and without contrast between animal and background. Classifiers can be trained from about 30 minutes of annotated video, and an annotated RGB-D dataset is released alongside the free software.

name: DeepBhvTracking
description: Deep-learning detection combined with background subtraction for rodent tracking
details: Tracks laboratory animals in video by first detecting them with a YOLO deep-learning detector trained on hand-labeled frames, then refining the body center with background subtraction inside each bounding box. The combination is aimed at difficult recordings with uneven lighting, tethered recording devices or experimenter interference. It outputs animal position over time and can be applied across behavioral paradigms and animal models.

name: ART (Automated Rodent Tracker)
description: Automated tracking of rodent position, body and nose in open-field video
details: Open-source tracker for open-field rodent video that automatically estimates the animal's position along with body and nose locations. It suits simple single-animal arena experiments where location and head direction are the main measures.

name: Pixying Behavior
description: Real-time and post hoc tracking of colour-marked body parts with Pixy cameras
details: Tracks color-marked body parts of animals using inexpensive Pixy cameras, which perform color-blob detection on board. It supports both real-time tracking during an experiment and post hoc analysis of recorded data.

name: ArUco marker scoring
description: Real-time engagement scoring from fiducial ArUco markers worn by rodents
details: Scores rat task engagement from ArUco fiducial markers worn by the animal and detected in video in real time. Developed for a nose-poke go/no-go task, it converts marker tracking into a two-state engaged versus distracted model and uses a sliding kernel to find when animals switch between states, helping set sensible session lengths.

name: Ethoscopes
description: Raspberry Pi platform for high-throughput real-time tracking of Drosophila
details: Combines 3D-printed hardware, Raspberry Pi computers and Arduino boards into scalable units for high-throughput behavioral monitoring, mainly of Drosophila. Each unit tracks and profiles behavior in real time with a supervised machine-learning approach and can deliver stimuli triggered by the animal's behavior in closed loop. Both hardware designs and software are open source and customizable.

name: BonZeb
description: Bonsai modules for high-resolution zebrafish tracking and closed-loop stimulation
details: A set of modular packages for the Bonsai visual programming environment that track larval zebrafish at high resolution, either online during experiments or offline in batch. It supports head-fixed closed-loop and free-swimming virtual open-loop assays, multi-animal tracking, and can be combined with optogenetic stimulation and calcium imaging, with little programming required.

name: Argus
description: R application for quantifying zebrafish behaviour from tracking data
details: An R application for quantifying zebrafish behavior from existing tracking data. It takes trajectories produced by a tracker and computes behavioral measures from them.

name: ZebraTrack
description: Low-cost imaging setup with ImageJ tracking of adult zebrafish
details: Pairs a low-cost imaging setup with ImageJ-based tracking for recording and analyzing the behavior of adult zebrafish. It is aimed at labs wanting an inexpensive, accessible way to obtain swimming trajectories.

name: JAABA
description: Supervised behavior classification from trajectories
details: Janelia's interactive tool for training supervised behavior classifiers from animal trajectories. Users label examples of a behavior in a graphical interface, and the software learns a classifier that can then annotate behavior automatically across large datasets. It is MATLAB-based and widely used with flies and rodents.

name: DeepEthogram
description: Supervised behavior classification from raw video
details: Converts raw video frames directly into an ethogram, labeling which user-defined behaviors occur in each frame, without needing pose estimation. Convolutional networks estimate motion, extract image and motion features and classify them into behaviors; it was demonstrated on mice and flies and handles rare behaviors with modest training data. A graphical interface lets users run the full pipeline without programming.

name: MARS
description: Pose estimation and social behavior classification in mice
details: An automated pipeline that estimates the pose of pairs of freely interacting mice and classifies their social behaviors from top-view video. Its pose and annotation training datasets are released as community benchmarks. It is paired with BENTO, a graphical interface for browsing behavior alongside other neuroscience data such as neural recordings.

name: BehaviorDEPOT
description: Pose-guided behavior detection and analysis
details: A MATLAB application with a graphical interface that turns markerless pose tracking output into behavior labels. It includes ready-made freezing and rearing classifiers that work with mice and rats wearing optogenetic cables or head-mounted miniscopes, modules for building ground-truth definitions and custom classifiers, and an Arduino-based module for running fear conditioning experiments. Outputs can be aligned with neural recordings.

name: LabGym
description: Tracking and behavior classification via Mask R-CNN
details: Detects and tracks animals in video, then identifies user-defined behaviors with customizable convolutional recurrent networks that look at both appearance and motion rather than a few hand-picked features. It reports quantitative measures of each behavior, including intensity and body kinematics, tracks multiple animals at once and requires no programming. It has been applied to species ranging from soft-bodied invertebrates to mammals.

name: SIPEC
description: End-to-end deep-learning behavioral analysis pipeline
details: An end-to-end deep-learning pipeline covering animal identification, tracking, pose estimation and behavior classification from video. It targets interacting primates and mice in complex environments.

name: DeepAction
description: Video-based behaviour classification with confidence-based review
details: A MATLAB toolbox that annotates animal behavior in video by extracting features from raw frames with a pretrained convolutional network and classifying them with a recurrent network. It assigns a confidence score to its predictions so users can prioritize which automatic annotations to review, and includes an annotation interface. It was evaluated on rodent and octopus video.

name: DLC2Action
description: Deep-learning behaviour segmentation from pose
details: A Python toolbox for automatic behavior segmentation from 2D or 3D pose tracking, video or audio data. It bundles several deep-learning action segmentation models, supports self-supervised pretraining to cope with limited labels, and provides benchmark datasets for model comparison. A graphical interface supports annotation, active learning and inspection of predictions, and many pose and annotation formats are accepted.

name: OpenLabCluster
description: Active-learning clustering and classification from keypoints
details: Groups segments of pose keypoint sequences into clusters and then uses active learning to pick representative segments for the user to label, so that a small number of annotations refines both clustering and behavior classification. It runs through an interactive graphical interface and is applicable to multiple animal species.

name: CBAS
description: Circadian behavioural analysis suite for long recordings
details: A pipeline for continuous, parallel video recording and real-time classification of home-cage behavior across many animals over days to weeks. It uses a self-supervised vision model to make classification robust to changing conditions and is geared toward analyzing circadian rhythms in behaviors such as digging and nesting in mice.

name: JABS
description: Pose pipeline and supervised classifier training for mice (JAX)
details: An integrated mouse phenotyping platform from The Jackson Laboratory combining open-field hardware designs and acquisition software, a pose-based active-learning tool for annotating behavior and training classifiers, and a web application for sharing classifiers. Trained classifiers can be applied to curated datasets spanning many mouse strains to support genetic analyses such as heritability.

name: LISBET
description: Transformer-based social behaviour segmentation from pose
details: A transformer model that detects and segments social interactions from body tracking data of interacting animals. Self-supervised pretraining reduces the need for manual labels, and it can be used for supervised classification, unsupervised discovery of behavioral motifs or phenotyping of individual mice.

name: FERAL
description: Supervised behaviour segmentation from raw video using video-understanding models; no pose required
details: Maps raw video directly to frame-level behavior labels using video-understanding models, so no pose estimation is needed. Trained with supervised labels, it handles behaviors from single-animal locomotion to social and collective dynamics across species and recording conditions. It is distributed as a user-friendly package that can run locally or on cloud servers.

name: PainFace-Recognition
description: Recurrent-network recognition of equine pain expressions from video
details: A deep recurrent two-stream network that distinguishes pain from non-pain in video of horses, using both appearance and motion over time. It was developed and evaluated on recordings of horses with experimentally induced moderate pain.

name: SaLSa
description: Semi-automatic labelling and LSTM classification of behaviours from pose (MATLAB)
details: A MATLAB approach for classifying behavioral syllables of mice in an open field from tracked body parts. Egocentric pose features are first clustered automatically to propose candidate syllables, which users confirm and label in a graphical interface; an LSTM network is then trained on these labels to classify the rest of the data.

name: B-SOiD
description: Unsupervised behavior discovery from pose
details: Discovers behaviors from pose estimation output without user-defined labels by clustering patterns in body-part positions and then training a classifier on those clusters, so new data can be processed quickly. It works with data from a single standard camera and also provides kinematic measures of limb trajectories, and it can be applied to any animal with tracked keypoints.

name: A-SOiD
description: Active-learning behavior classification from pose
details: An active-learning platform that classifies behavior from pose data with expert guidance, iteratively asking the user to label the most informative samples so classifiers can be trained with less annotation. It can also help discover new behaviors and applies to multiple species.

name: Keypoint-MoSeq
description: Unsupervised behavioral syllable discovery from keypoints
details: Splits continuous keypoint tracking data into discrete behavioral syllables without supervision. A generative model separates tracking jitter from real movement so syllable boundaries match natural transitions in pose. It works on standard 2D or 3D keypoints from common trackers, has been applied to mice and flies, and handles both solitary and social behavior.

name: VAME
description: Unsupervised behavioral motif discovery from pose
details: An unsupervised deep-learning framework that learns embeddings of pose trajectories with a variational autoencoder and segments them into discrete behavioral motifs. Motifs are further organized into hierarchical communities, allowing comparison of motif usage between experimental groups. It was demonstrated on mice and is applicable to many experimental setups.

name: DeepOF
description: Behavioral analysis of DeepLabCut/SLEAP tracking
details: A Python package for analyzing mouse pose tracking from DeepLabCut or SLEAP. It offers supervised annotation of predefined behaviors, including social interactions, as well as unsupervised discovery of behavioral patterns from motion tracking data.

name: TREBA
description: Trajectory embeddings for behavior representation learning
details: Learns compact embeddings of animal trajectories through self-supervised learning guided by programmed tasks that encode expert knowledge. These embeddings serve as features for downstream behavior classifiers and reduce the number of manual annotations needed. It was evaluated on mouse and fruit fly tracking data.

name: MotionMapper
description: Unsupervised behavioral mapping from postural dynamics
details: Maps an animal's postural dynamics into a low-dimensional behavioral space and identifies stereotyped behaviors as dense regions in that space, without predefined labels. It was developed on video of freely walking fruit flies, where it revealed many distinct locomotion and grooming states, and is implemented in MATLAB.

name: MoSeq
description: Depth-video behavioral syllable segmentation
details: Motion Sequencing segments mouse behavior into brief, reusable modules called syllables from depth camera video, without supervision. The moseq2 application provides a pipeline for extracting the mouse from 3D depth recordings, fitting the model and comparing syllable usage across groups.

name: SEB3R
description: Segmentation of mouse body language into postures linked to stimulus-evoked emotional behaviour
details: Combines machine-learning pose tracking with unsupervised clustering to identify distinct body postures in freely moving mice on a sub-second scale. It was developed for stimulus-evoked tests such as whisker stimulation, where the identified postures serve as indicators of fearful versus exploratory responses.

name: DLC2Kinematics
description: Kinematic quantities from DeepLabCut pose output
details: A Python package that computes kinematic quantities, such as velocities, accelerations and joint angles, from DeepLabCut pose estimation output. It is useful for movement analysis once keypoints have been tracked.

name: traja
description: Trajectory analysis and visualisation built on pandas
details: A Python package for analyzing and visualizing animal trajectories that extends pandas data frames with trajectory methods. It provides feature extraction, statistical modeling and plotting for time series of positions and is suited to non-video sources such as home-cage tracking as well as pose output. It interoperates with related spatial analysis tools in Python and R.

name: PyRat
description: Python library for behavioural and trajectory analysis of pose data
details: A Python library for analyzing rodent pose tracking data, computing distance traveled, speed and area occupancy. It clusters behaviors with unsupervised methods such as hierarchical clustering and t-SNE and can link detected behaviors with synchronized neural recordings for visualization.

name: animovement
description: R toolbox for analysing movement across space and time
details: An R toolbox for analyzing animal movement across space and time. It processes tracking data into movement and trajectory measures for downstream analysis.

name: Rtrack
description: Unbiased search-strategy classification for water-maze and related assays
details: An R package for analyzing spatial exploration in tests such as the Morris water maze. It imports tracking data, computes and visualizes path measures and classifies search strategies with a parameter-free machine-learning model, and proposes a standard export format for sharing data across platforms.

name: ColonyTrack
description: Analysis of long-term tracking data from group-housed colonies
details: An R package for analyzing long-term tracking data from group-housed animal colonies. It summarizes how individuals move and use space in the shared enclosure over extended periods.

name: swaRm
description: R package for individual and collective movement metrics
details: An R package for computing movement metrics of individual animals and of groups from trajectory data. It is suited to studies of collective behavior where interactions within a group are of interest.

name: LocoMouse
description: Markerless tracking of paws, nose and tail for whole-body locomotor coordination
details: Markerless video system that tracks the paws, nose and tail of freely walking mice to quantify limb, head and tail kinematics. Beyond single-paw trajectories, it measures interlimb and whole-body coordination in 3D, making it suited to characterizing gait ataxia, for example in mice with cerebellar circuit defects. Open source.

name: LocoWhisk / ARTv2
description: Combined whisker movement and locomotion analysis in rodents
details: Open-source tool for analyzing whisker movements together with locomotion in rodents, so that whisking and gait can be studied in the same recordings.

name: Whisker Tracker
description: Whisker tracking, released with an open high-speed infrared video database of freely moving rodents
details: MATLAB-based tool for tracking whisker and nose positions in high-speed infrared video of freely moving rats and mice. It is released alongside a large open video dataset of juvenile and adult rodents exploring an object on a gap-crossing task, recorded under varied lighting and contrast, with a hand-tracked subset that can serve as ground truth for testing image-processing and machine-learning methods.

name: KineMouse Wheel
description: Transparent running wheel for 3D head-fixed locomotion tracking with one camera
details: Open hardware design for a transparent running wheel that lets a single camera capture head-fixed mouse locomotion for 3D kinematic tracking. It was developed for machine-learning-based kinematic analysis of how mice adjust their stepping when they detect obstacles with their whiskers.

name: ReachOut
description: Hardware and software for recording and analysing mouse reach-to-grasp
details: Open-source combination of hardware and software for running and recording a mouse reach-to-grasp task and analyzing the resulting forelimb reaching movements from video.

name: MouseMove
description: Semi-automated movement and cognitive analysis of open-field tracks
details: Open-source software for semi-automated analysis of open-field tracking data, extracting both locomotor (movement) measures and cognitive or exploratory measures from previously recorded animal tracks.

name: Pathfinder
description: Classifies spatial navigation search strategies in water mazes and similar tasks
details: Open-source tool that takes animal tracking paths from water mazes and similar spatial navigation tasks and classifies each trial into a search strategy, giving a richer readout than latency or distance alone.

name: STL toolbox
description: Spectral time-lapse summaries of movement from pre-recorded video
details: MATLAB toolbox that turns pre-recorded video of an animal in an open arena into a single summary image, coloring its position at each time point by time and overlaying it on a reference frame. It also includes automated motion tracking to compute path length, duration, instantaneous velocity and acceleration, with many user-adjustable settings.

name: DBscorer
description: Automated immobility scoring in forced-swim and tail-suspension tests
details: Windows program with a graphical interface that scores immobility from video of the forced swim and tail suspension tests used in rodent depression and antidepressant research. Users calibrate parameters for their setup, and the output includes total immobility time plus time-resolved mobility and immobility plots showing how behavioral despair develops over a session.

name: MOVE
description: Motion analysis of conditioned fear and other video-recorded tests
details: Open-source motion-analysis software for video-recorded behavioral tests, aimed primarily at quantifying freezing and movement in conditioned fear experiments.

name: LMT-toolkit
description: Web application for analysing Live Mouse Tracker data
details: Open-source web application for analyzing the databases produced by Live Mouse Tracker, the multi-mouse home-cage tracking system, so that users can extract and summarize individual and social behavior measures without writing analysis scripts.

name: Detectron2
description: Object detection and instance segmentation library
details: Python library built on PyTorch for training and running object detection and instance segmentation models. In behavior research it is used to detect and segment animals or objects in video frames, producing bounding boxes and pixel masks that can feed downstream tracking.

name: Segment Anything (SAM 2)
description: Promptable image and video segmentation
details: Promptable foundation model that segments objects in images and videos from simple prompts such as clicks or boxes, then propagates the masks through video using a streaming memory. For behavior studies it can produce animal or object masks across frames with little manual annotation; code, model weights and training data are publicly released.

name: DeepSqueak
description: Deep-learning detection and classification of USVs
details: Open-source deep-learning software for detecting and classifying ultrasonic vocalizations (USVs) in rodent audio recordings.

name: DAS (Deep Audio Segmenter)
description: Deep-learning annotation of acoustic signals
details: Deep-learning tool that segments and labels acoustic signals, such as syllables or sound pulses, in recordings from insects, birds and mammals. A graphical interface supports manual annotation, network training and proofreading of predictions; new species can be learned from a modest amount of labeled data, and its low latency allows real-time annotation for closed-loop experiments.

name: USVSEG
description: Segmentation of rodent ultrasonic vocalisations
details: Signal-processing tool that detects rodent ultrasonic vocalization segments in continuous, noisy audio recorded during social behavior. It suppresses background-noise variation in the spectrogram to separate calls, and tracks the spectral peak over time within each syllable; it has been applied to vocalizations from several rodent species.

name: MUPET
description: Mouse ultrasonic profile extraction and syllable clustering
details: Open-source tool for analyzing mouse ultrasonic vocalizations, extracting syllables from recordings and clustering them by spectral shape to build and compare vocal repertoires.

name: VocalMat
description: Detection and classification of mouse vocalisations
details: Software that detects mouse ultrasonic vocalizations in audio files using image-processing methods applied to spectrograms, without requiring user-set detection parameters. Detected calls are then sorted into syllable categories with a machine-learning classifier, and dimensionality reduction is used to compare vocal repertoires across experimental groups.

name: AVA
description: Unsupervised latent-space analysis of vocal repertoires
details: Python package that learns compact features of vocalizations directly from spectrograms using a variational autoencoder, rather than relying on hand-picked acoustic measures. The learned latent space can be used to visualize, compare and quantify variability in vocal repertoires; it was demonstrated on laboratory mouse ultrasonic calls and zebra finch song.

name: Avisoft SASLab
description: Bioacoustic recording and sound analysis
details: Commercial bioacoustics software for recording and analyzing animal sounds, widely used for spectrogram-based measurement of rodent ultrasonic vocalizations. It is part of a larger product line that also includes ultrasound recording hardware.

name: USVCAM
description: Acoustic camera that localises ultrasonic vocalizations to individual mice
details: Acoustic camera system that localizes ultrasonic vocalizations and assigns each call to an individual mouse, using a compact microphone array combined with video instead of a distributed microphone setup. It includes USV segmentation adapted for overlapping calls and works in a conventional home cage, enabling analysis of vocal interactions during social tests such as resident-intruder.

name: NeuroMotive
description: Video tracking synchronised to Blackrock neural acquisition, for event-aligned and closed-loop analysis
details: Commercial video-tracking system from Blackrock Neurotech that records animal position synchronized with Blackrock neural acquisition hardware. Tracking data share a common timebase with the neural recordings, supporting event-aligned analysis and closed-loop experiments.

name: Implantable telemetry
description: Implanted physiological telemetry (blood pressure, ECG) in freely moving animals (DSI)
details: Commercial implantable telemetry from Data Sciences International (DSI) that records physiological signals such as blood pressure and ECG from freely moving animals. These data can be aligned with behavioral recordings to relate physiology to behavior without tethering the animal.

name: GuPPy
description: Fiber photometry analysis in Python
details: Free Python program for analyzing fiber photometry recordings from freely behaving animals, accepting data from a range of acquisition systems. Users load data and set parameters through graphical interfaces rather than code, and it produces exportable plots of signals aligned to behavioral or task events; it runs across operating systems and can be extended by Python users.

name: pMAT
description: Photometry modular analysis tool
details: Open-source modular tool for analyzing fiber photometry data, including aligning photometry signals to behavioral events.

name: CaImAn
description: Calcium imaging motion correction and source extraction
details: Open-source Python library for calcium imaging analysis that handles motion correction, identification of active neurons and extraction of their activity traces, and registration of cells across sessions. It works with both two-photon and one-photon data, scales from laptops to computing clusters, and can analyze streaming data in real time.

name: suite2p
description: Calcium imaging processing and cell detection
details: Python pipeline for two-photon calcium imaging that registers raw movies, detects active cells, extracts their fluorescence traces and infers spike times. It runs on standard workstations, processes data faster than real time, and is designed to handle very large neuron populations.

name: Minian
description: Miniscope calcium imaging analysis pipeline
details: Open-source Python pipeline for extracting cell locations, calcium traces and deconvolved activity from single-photon miniscope recordings in freely behaving animals. Each processing step comes with interactive visualizations for choosing and checking parameters, and its modest memory needs allow it to run on a laptop, making it accessible to users with limited programming experience.

name: neurotic
description: Synchronised browsing and annotation of neural signals and behaviour video
details: Open-source Python application for reviewing and annotating electrophysiological signals synchronized with behavior video. It supports many file formats, performs basic analyses such as filtering, spike detection and burst detection, and uses a portable configuration file that describes how datasets are located, loaded and plotted, which eases sharing with collaborators.

name: CAVE
description: Combined analysis of head-mounted calcium imaging and behaviour video (MATLAB)
details: MATLAB program for analyzing head-mounted miniscope calcium imaging alongside simultaneously recorded behavior video in freely moving rodents. It provides motion correction and automatic ROI detection with manual refinement, tracks the animal's position and orientation, and lets users relate neural activity to behavioral epochs and external events through a workflow aimed at novice users.

name: OpenSync
description: Synchronises video, physiological and behavioural data streams
details: Open-source framework for recording and synchronizing multiple data streams, such as video, physiological signals and behavioral measures, on a common timeline.

name: movement
description: Analysis of pose tracks from DeepLabCut, SLEAP, and others
details: Python toolbox for loading, cleaning, filtering and analyzing pose-tracking output from tools such as DeepLabCut and SLEAP in a common data format. It computes kinematic variables from keypoint trajectories and is species- and tool-agnostic.

name: NWB
description: Neurodata Without Borders standard for neurophysiology data
details: Neurodata Without Borders is an open data standard and software ecosystem for storing neurophysiology data and metadata, covering electrophysiology, optical recordings and associated behavior across species. Using a shared format makes datasets easier to exchange, archive, reuse and analyze with compatible tools.

name: ndx-pose
description: NWB extension for storing pose-estimation data
details: Extension to the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard that defines how to store pose-estimation results, such as keypoint coordinates, confidence scores and skeleton definitions, alongside neural and other experimental data in NWB files.

name: DLC-Analyzer
description: Analysis and visualization of DeepLabCut output
details: R-based toolkit for post-processing DeepLabCut keypoint output from classic rodent tests such as the open field, elevated plus maze and forced swim test. It computes tracking metrics and zone-based measures and supports supervised machine-learning classifiers trained on manual annotations to score ethologically relevant behaviors, offering an alternative to commercial tracking platforms.

name: DeepLabCut-Live
description: Real-time pose estimation on live video
details: Python package for running trained DeepLabCut models on live video with low latency, so that posture can trigger external hardware in closed-loop experiments. It includes a forward-prediction option to compensate for processing delay and dynamic cropping to speed inference, and can be used through a standalone GUI or within Bonsai and AutoPilot.

name: DeepLabStream
description: Real-time, closed-loop pose-based feedback
details: Closed-loop system that estimates mouse posture from live video in real time and triggers stimuli or devices when defined postures or behaviors occur. It supports different input and output devices and can be adapted to various experimental designs, such as posture-triggered optogenetics or semi-autonomous conditioning tasks with freely moving mice.

name: Bonsai
description: Visual reactive programming for experiment pipelines
details: Open-source visual programming environment for acquiring and processing parallel data streams online, where users build experiment pipelines by connecting nodes rather than writing code. It is commonly used to combine cameras, video tracking of behavior, electrophysiology and other hardware, and to implement closed-loop stimulation.

name: AMBER-pipeline
description: Automated rodent maternal-behavior analysis
details: Open-source pipeline for automatically scoring maternal and dam-pup interactions in home-cage video of rats during the first postnatal days. It uses DeepLabCut models to track keypoints on the dam and individual pups, then SimBA random forest classifiers to label behaviors such as active and passive nursing, nest attendance, licking and grooming, self-grooming, eating and drinking, without special housing or proprietary software.

name: AmadeusGPT
description: Natural-language querying of behaviour from pose data
details: Natural-language interface that turns plain-language descriptions of behavior into executable analysis code using large language models, so users can query pose-estimation and video data without programming. Generated code draws on built-in modules for machine learning, computer vision, spatiotemporal reasoning and visualization, and results can be refined interactively across species.

name: Pyper
description: Real-time or offline open-field tracking with TTL output on region entry
details: Open-source Python software for tracking a single animal in open-field video, either live from a camera or offline from recorded files. It can emit a TTL signal when the animal enters a user-defined region, allowing tracking to trigger external hardware in closed-loop experiments.

name: Oat
description: Modular real-time animal tracking and video processing programs
details: A set of modular, open-source programs for real-time animal tracking and video processing. Separate components handle tasks such as frame acquisition, filtering, position detection and recording, and can be chained together into a custom pipeline for live experiments.

name: RAT (Rodent Arena Tracker)
description: Machine-vision camera for closed-loop rodent tracking and task control
details: A pocket-sized, low-cost tracker built on the open-source OpenMV machine-vision camera that follows a rodent's position in real time without a tethered computer. It logs timestamped x/y coordinates to an onboard microSD card instead of saving video, and a programmable input/output pin lets it control or exchange signals with other equipment, for example to drive optogenetic stimulation in real-time place preference tasks. Design files, build instructions and code are openly available.

name: Open Ephys tracking plugin
description: Behavioural tracking and closed-loop stimulation built on Open Ephys
details: A plugin for the open-source Open Ephys electrophysiology acquisition system that adds behavioral position tracking. Tracking data are recorded alongside neural signals and can be used to trigger closed-loop stimulation.

name: CLARA
description: Closed-loop automated reaching apparatus with real-time DeepLabCut
details: A closed-loop reaching apparatus for mice that uses real-time DeepLabCut pose estimation to track skilled reaching in 3D without physical markers. It automates trial initiation and pellet delivery, classifies reach outcomes from the kinematics, and can deliver neural stimulation, such as vagus nerve stimulation, with low latency depending on whether a reach succeeds. It is designed to work alongside neurophysiology recording tools.

name: Phenopy
description: Python platform for home-cage behavioural phenotyping and data sharing
details: A Python-based platform for behavioral phenotyping in the home cage, with an emphasis on organizing and sharing behavioral data.

name: BORIS
description: Event-logging and manual video annotation
details: A free, open-source, cross-platform program for manually coding behavior from recorded videos or live observation. Users define a project ethogram of state and point events, assign them to keyboard keys, and score any number of subjects, with up to two synchronized videos per observation. It produces time budgets and event plots and exports data in common formats such as CSV, spreadsheet and JSON.

name: Solomon Coder
description: Manual behavior coding tool
details: A freeware desktop tool for manually coding behavior from video. Users score behaviors over the course of a recording and export the resulting annotations for analysis.

name: Noldus Observer XT
description: Manual behavior annotation suite
details: Commercial software from Noldus for manual behavior annotation and event logging. It supports defining coding schemes, scoring behaviors over time from video, and summarizing the annotated events for analysis.

name: CVAT
description: Image and video annotation for detection, segmentation, and keypoints
details: An open-source, web-based tool for annotating images and video. It supports bounding boxes, polygon segmentation masks and keypoints, making it useful for creating training data for animal detection, segmentation and pose-estimation models.

name: Label Studio
description: Multi-type data labeling and annotation platform
details: An open-source, general-purpose data labeling platform that handles many data types, including images, video, audio and text. Labeling interfaces can be customized, and it is commonly used to prepare training datasets for machine learning models.

name: VIA (VGG Image Annotator)
description: Lightweight image, audio, and video annotation tool
details: A lightweight manual annotation tool from the Oxford Visual Geometry Group that runs entirely offline in a web browser with no installation. Annotators can mark spatial regions in images or video frames and temporal segments in audio or video, then export the results as JSON or CSV. It also supports collaborative labeling of large datasets by teams.

name: Labelme
description: Polygon, bounding-box, and keypoint image annotation; SimBA converts its labels to YOLO and DeepLabCut training data
details: An open-source desktop tool for drawing polygons, bounding boxes and keypoints on images. SimBA can convert its annotations into training data for YOLO and DeepLabCut models, making it a convenient route to custom detection and pose-estimation datasets.

name: ELAN
description: Time-aligned annotation of video and audio
details: Open-source software from the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics for creating time-aligned annotations on video and audio recordings. Annotations are organized on multiple tiers, which suits detailed coding of overlapping behaviors or vocalizations.

name: BENTO
description: Synchronised annotation of behaviour, pose, and neural traces
details: An open-source MATLAB-based interface for annotating behavior while viewing video, pose-estimation tracks and neural recordings in sync. It is aimed at experiments that combine behavior with neural data, letting users browse and label multiple data streams on a shared timeline.

name: EnVision
description: Imaging embedded in Allentown IVC racks; individual behaviour from group-housed mice (The Jackson Laboratory)
details: A commercial home-cage monitoring system from The Jackson Laboratory with cameras embedded in Allentown individually ventilated cage racks. It records group-housed mice continuously in their home cages and extracts behavior for individual animals.

name: DOME smart lids
description: Camera lid retrofitted to existing racks; computer-vision keypoints, multi-animal via purpose-made ear tags (Olden Labs)
details: Commercial camera lids from Olden Labs that retrofit onto existing cage racks and record near-infrared video and audio from the home cage. Computer vision extracts body keypoints, and purpose-made ear tags allow individual animals to be distinguished when several share a cage.

name: iMouse
description: Rack-mounted side-view cameras with proprietary ML; retrofits standard cages (iMouse GmbH)
details: A commercial home-cage monitoring system from iMouse GmbH that uses rack-mounted side-view cameras and retrofits standard cages without disrupting facility workflows. Users can remotely observe, record, share and review home-cage video, and proprietary machine learning detects specific behaviors such as drinking, and how long they last, within user-defined zones.

name: PhenoTyper
description: Instrumented home cage for up to two rodents; pairs with EthoVision XT (Noldus)
details: An instrumented home cage from Noldus for one or two rodents, recorded with infrared video so behavior can be monitored around the clock. It is designed to be used with EthoVision XT for tracking and behavioral analysis.

name: PhenoRack
description: 24/7 home-cage activity for up to 32 individually housed animals (Viewpoint)
details: A commercial video-based system from Viewpoint for continuous 24/7 home-cage activity monitoring of up to 32 individually housed animals.

name: HomeCageScan / PhenoCube
description: Automated recognition of unconstrained home-cage behaviours; individually housed (CleverSys)
details: Commercial software from CleverSys that automatically recognizes a range of unconstrained behaviors from video of individually housed rodents in their home cages.

name: BlackBox
description: Postural dynamics, gait and weight distribution from video; single-housed (BlackBox Bio)
details: A commercial system from BlackBox Bio that measures postural dynamics, gait and weight distribution from video of single-housed rodents.

name: Trackpaw
description: Non-invasive in-cage weight, activity and respiratory metrics in mice (TrackPaw Scientific)
details: A commercial system from TrackPaw Scientific that measures body weight, activity and respiratory metrics in mice non-invasively inside the cage.

name: BioSyft
description: Automated behavioural analytics for preclinical rodent research (BioSyft)
details: A commercial video-based platform from BioSyft offering automated behavioral analytics for preclinical rodent research.

name: SmartCage System
description: All-in-one automated home-cage recording and activity monitoring (MazeEngineers)
details: A commercial all-in-one home cage from MazeEngineers that combines video with infrared beam breaks for automated recording and activity monitoring.

name: Vium Digital Vivarium
description: Smart housing with continuous video and computer-vision digital biomarkers; acquired by Recursion in 2020 and no longer sold (Vium)
details: A smart-housing system that combined continuous home-cage video with sensors and computer vision to derive digital biomarkers of rodent behavior. Vium was acquired by Recursion in 2020 and the system is no longer sold.

name: AVERT
description: Continuous home-cage video with 24-hour ultrasonic vocalization recording (MRC Harwell)
details: A home-cage monitoring setup from MRC Harwell that pairs continuous video recording with 24-hour ultrasonic vocalization recording, so behavior and vocal activity are captured together.

name: Raspberry Rat
description: Open-source Raspberry Pi platform for scheduled home-cage video recording and cloud upload
details: An open-source, Raspberry Pi based platform for recording home-cage video on a schedule and uploading the footage to cloud storage, offering a low-cost route to long-term video collection.

name: Dual Cage
description: Automated home cage for avoidance and risk-assessment testing; no longer sold (Biobserve)
details: A commercial automated home cage from Biobserve for avoidance and risk-assessment testing in rodents, monitored by video. It is no longer sold.

name: Automated Figure-8 Maze
description: Home-cage-attached delayed-alternation maze for longitudinal working memory; no longer sold (Biobserve)
details: A commercial figure-8 maze from Biobserve that attaches to the home cage and runs a delayed-alternation task for measuring working memory longitudinally, monitored by video. It is no longer sold.

name: Home Cage Analyser (HCA)
description: Individual metrics from socially housed mice or rats; three animals optimal (Actual Analytics)
details: A commercial system from Actual Analytics that combines RFID identification with infrared video to produce individual behavioral metrics for socially housed mice or rats. It works best with about three animals per cage.

name: IntelliCage
description: Home-cage behaviour and cognitive testing for up to 16 mice or 8 rats (TSE Systems)
details: A commercial home-cage system from TSE Systems that identifies group-housed animals by RFID and records their nose-pokes and licks. It supports automated behavioral and cognitive testing for up to 16 mice or 8 rats per cage.

name: ColonyRack
description: Rack-scale tracking of individual animals in large, semi-natural groups (PhenoSys)
details: A commercial rack-scale system from PhenoSys that uses RFID to track individual animals living in large, semi-natural groups.

name: M3 MultiMouseMonitor
description: Real-time position of individual animals within a group cage (PhenoSys)
details: A commercial RFID system from PhenoSys that reports the real-time position of each individual animal within a group cage.

name: UID Mouse Matrix
description: Continuous temperature, locomotor activity and zone preference per animal (Unified Information Devices)
details: A commercial RFID platform from Unified Information Devices that continuously records body temperature, locomotor activity and zone preference for each animal in a cage.

name: AnyCage Lite
description: Continuous non-invasive body temperature via UCT-2112 microchips; single-cage and small-cohort studies (Unified Information Devices)
details: A commercial RFID setup from Unified Information Devices that continuously and non-invasively records body temperature from implanted UCT-2112 microchips. It is aimed at single-cage and small-cohort studies.

name: HomeLab
description: Unique animal IDs tracked across connected cages; mice (NeuroCage)
details: A commercial system from NeuroCage that tracks unique RFID animal IDs across connected cages, combining RFID with networked (IoT) hardware for monitoring mice.

name: UCT-2112 temperature microchip
description: Implantable chip returning ID and body temperature on a single scan; a component rather than a system (Unified Information Devices)
details: An implantable passive RFID microchip from Unified Information Devices that returns both the animal's ID and its body temperature on a single scan. It is a component used with compatible readers rather than a full monitoring system.

name: Eco-HAB
description: Four-compartment RFID system for social behaviour and hierarchy in group-housed mice; open source
details: An open-source RFID system for group-housed mice made up of four connected compartments. Each animal's movements between compartments are logged and used to assess social behavior and dominance hierarchy.

name: MoPSS
description: Mouse Position Surveillance System: RFID position tracking in the home cage; open source
details: The Mouse Position Surveillance System is an open-source RFID setup for tracking the positions of individual mice in the home cage over time.

name: Automated Visible Burrow System
description: Burrow-style colony cage with RFID and video tracking; open cage design and analysis scripts
details: A colony cage built around a burrow-style layout in which group-housed rodents are monitored with combined RFID identification and video tracking. Animals are tagged so individual identities can be followed within the group over time. The cage design and accompanying analysis scripts are openly shared, making it suited to labs studying social and home-cage behavior in naturalistic group settings.

name: DVC (Digital Ventilated Cage)
description: 24/7 locomotion and environmental metrics read from the rack itself, at cage level (Tecniplast)
details: A Tecniplast rack system that records locomotion and cage environment around the clock using an electronic sensing board built into the rack itself, without cameras or changes to the cage. Measurements are made at the cage level rather than per animal, giving continuous activity data for mice housed in standard individually ventilated cages.

name: LABORAS
description: Behaviour classified from vibration and force signals for up to eight solitary animals (Metris)
details: A Metris platform that places each cage on a sensing base and classifies behavior from the vibration and force signals the animal produces, with no video required. It supports up to eight singly housed animals at once and outputs automated behavior scores and activity measures over long recordings.

name: InfraMot
description: Total activity from radiated body heat via a lid sensor; now a PhenoMaster NG module (TSE Systems)
details: A TSE Systems sensor mounted on the cage lid that measures total activity by detecting the body heat an animal radiates, using passive infrared. It gives a simple, continuous activity readout without video and is now offered as a module within the PhenoMaster NG platform.

name: Mouse E-Motion
description: Single-animal movement plus cage temperature, humidity and light (INFRA-E-MOTION)
details: A compact infrared device from INFRA-E-MOTION that logs the movement of a single animal in its home cage. Alongside activity it also records cage temperature, humidity and light, so behavior can be related to environmental conditions over long periods.

name: Actimeter
description: Locomotor activity, circadian rhythm and novelty reactivity; individually housed (Imetronic)
details: An Imetronic infrared system for individually housed rodents that measures locomotor activity over time. It is used to study circadian rhythms and the animal's reaction to novelty, producing activity counts rather than video-based behavior labels.

name: Activity Cage
description: Horizontal and vertical (rearing) activity for individuals or groups (Ugo Basile)
details: An Ugo Basile cage fitted with an infrared beam frame that counts horizontal movement and vertical activity such as rearing. It can be used with single animals or groups and produces beam-break based activity measures without video tracking.

name: Pallidus MR1
description: Cage-level temperature, light, humidity and activity reported over LoRaWAN (Pallidus Sensing)
details: A wireless sensor from Pallidus Sensing that attaches at the cage level and reports temperature, light, humidity and animal activity. Data are sent over a LoRaWAN network, allowing remote monitoring of many cages without cabling or cameras.

name: MOSHERS
description: Individual food intake in group-housed mice; NC3Rs CRACK IT challenge (Research Devices)
details: Smart food hoppers from Research Devices, developed through the NC3Rs CRACK IT challenge, that combine a camera with AI to measure how much each mouse eats while living in a group. This gives individual food intake data without having to single-house animals.

name: SmartWaiter
description: Feeding and drinking patterns at cage level (Cibertec)
details: A Cibertec automatic feeder system that records feeding and drinking patterns in the home cage. Measurements are made at the cage level, providing time-resolved intake data rather than video-based behavior analysis.

name: COMPASS
description: Continuous activity and sleep monitoring from passive-infrared sensors; open source
details: An open-source approach that uses passive infrared sensors to monitor activity continuously in the home cage and to estimate sleep from periods of immobility. It offers a low-cost, non-invasive alternative to video or EEG for long-term activity and sleep recording in rodents.

name: Actifield
description: Open-source automated actimeter for rodents
details: An open-source, automated actimeter for rodents that measures locomotor activity using infrared beams. Published as open hardware, it can be built in-house as an inexpensive alternative to commercial activity monitors.

name: Microwave motion detector
description: Low-cost radar-based home-cage activity detector; open source
details: A low-cost, open-source home-cage activity detector that senses movement with microwave radar rather than cameras or beam breaks. It produces continuous activity readings for rodents in their cages and can be built from inexpensive components.

name: Open Face Home Cage Running Wheel
description: Open-source home-cage running wheel with logging
details: A 3D-printable, open-faced running wheel for mice that sits in the home cage and automatically logs distance, wheel direction and velocity. Data can be binned into epochs across a day or several days and collected remotely to avoid disturbing the animals, making it suited to exercise, metabolism and activity-based anorexia studies.

name: Low-Profile Wireless Running Wheel
description: Wireless running wheel that fits standard IVCs (Med Associates)
details: A Med Associates running wheel designed to fit inside standard individually ventilated cages. It records wheel-running activity wirelessly, allowing long-term home-cage locomotion measurement without cabling.

name: ClockLab
description: Circadian activity monitoring with running wheels and motion sensors (Actimetrics)
details: An Actimetrics system for circadian research that collects activity from running wheels and infrared motion sensors. It records long-term activity data and provides analysis of daily rhythms, such as actograms and period estimates, for rodents in their home cages.

name: MyVivarium
description: Open-source colony management with real-time cage environment sensing
details: An open-source, cloud-hosted web application for managing research-animal colonies, where cages are linked to database records through QR codes that can be scanned on mobile devices. Lab members can track individual animals and receive task reminders, and an accompanying low-cost sensor kit streams room humidity, temperature, light and vivarium worker activity into the database in real time.

name: FED3
description: Home-cage feeding device that measures food intake and runs operant tasks
details: An open-source, battery-powered pellet dispenser that sits in rodent home cages and records food intake over days or weeks with little experimenter involvement. Its nose-poke ports also let it run operant tasks to measure food motivation, and a programmable output allows syncing with optogenetic stimulation or neural recordings.

name: Sipper
description: Home-cage two-bottle-choice lick detection; SipperViz for analysis
details: A low-cost, open-source photobeam lickometer that fits inside standard home cages and measures intake from two bottles at once for preference tests. It is battery powered and wireless, has been combined with fiber photometry, and comes with SipperViz software for analyzing the drinking data.

name: LIQ HD
description: Lick-level drinking measurement across many home cages
details: An open-source lickometer that uses capacitive sensors to detect individual licks in two-bottle choice tasks in ventilated home cages. A single Arduino controls recordings across many cages for several days, logging to an SD card, and a touchscreen interface makes it usable without coding. Output supports analysis of preference over time and lick bout microstructure.

name: FARESHARE
description: Drinking microstructure of individual socially housed rodents
details: An open-source device that combines RFID with custom lick-sensing hardware to measure each animal's fluid intake when rats are housed together and share a drinking source. It timestamps every drinking bout, giving daily intake, preference, circadian patterns and lick microstructure per individual, and was developed for two-bottle-choice alcohol studies.

name: PiDose
description: Automated oral drug dosing of individual group-housed mice
details: An open-source module attached to the home cage that identifies group-housed mice by RFID, weighs each animal and delivers a bodyweight-adjusted daily drug dose through a drinking spout. It allows oral drug treatment over weeks to months without injection or gavage and with minimal handling.

subsection: Automated testing and training in the home cage
name: HASRA
description: Individualised skilled-reaching training of group-housed mice
details: An open-source system for training and testing group-housed mice on single-pellet skilled reaching inside their home cage. Mice visit an attached chamber where a motorized pedestal presents seeds to either forelimb, with RFID identifying each animal and video capturing reaches. It is used to track fine motor learning and deficits such as those after stroke.

subsection: Automated testing and training in the home cage
name: DIY-NAMIC
description: High-throughput operant phenotyping in the home cage
details: An open-source, inexpensive modular system for running standard operant paradigms directly in the rodent home cage using nose-poke ports and lick detection. Because animals test themselves, training can proceed faster, without food restriction and with far less daily experimenter effort, which makes it useful for time-limited windows such as adolescence.

subsection: Automated testing and training in the home cage
name: Home-cage mesoscale imaging
description: Self-initiated head fixation for task training and cortical imaging in the home cage
details: An open-source setup in which mice identified by RFID voluntarily enter a station attached to the home cage and self-initiate head fixation. This allows automated task training and widefield cortical imaging to be carried out repeatedly without experimenter handling.

name: PhenoMaster NG
description: Indirect calorimetry with activity, feeding and drinking; single or RFID-based social housing (TSE Systems)
details: A TSE Systems metabolic cage platform that combines indirect calorimetry with infrared-frame activity tracking and feeding and drinking measurement. Animals can be housed singly or socially with RFID identification, giving metabolic and behavioral data from the same recording.

name: Promethion
description: Continuous oxygen, carbon dioxide, water vapour, methane and stable-isotope measurement in rodents (Sable Systems)
details: A Sable Systems metabolic phenotyping system for rodents that continuously measures oxygen, carbon dioxide and water vapor, and can also measure methane and stable isotopes. It is used to quantify energy expenditure and respiratory gas exchange over long recordings.

name: Promethion Core
description: Metabolic data synchronised to behavioural events; single-housed (Sable Systems)
details: A Sable Systems metabolic cage system for singly housed rodents that records indirect calorimetry and synchronizes the metabolic data with behavioral events. This lets researchers relate energy expenditure to specific activities such as feeding or movement.

name: Oxymax-CLAMS
description: Energy expenditure in mice and rats; single or group housing depending on cage type (Columbus Instruments)
details: A Columbus Instruments indirect calorimetry system that measures energy expenditure in mice and rats. Depending on the cage type, animals can be housed singly or in groups.

name: Ethovision XT
description: Video tracking and analysis
details: A widely used commercial package from Noldus that tracks animals in video recordings and analyzes their movement and behavior. It supports a broad range of standard behavioral tests and outputs measures such as distance traveled, zone visits and movement-based behaviors, all through a graphical interface that needs no coding.

name: CatWalk XT
description: Gait analysis platform
details: A commercial gait analysis platform from Noldus in which rodents walk voluntarily across an illuminated glass walkway while a camera records their footprints from below. It produces quantitative measures of paw placement and gait, used for example in studies of pain and motor or neurological impairment.

name: ANY-maze
description: Video tracking and automated behavioural testing (Stoelting)
details: A commercial video tracking package from Stoelting for automated analysis of animal behavior in standard tests such as mazes and open fields. It works from live or recorded video, can control test apparatus, and produces movement and zone-based measures through a graphical interface.

name: CleverSys TopScan
description: Automated behaviour recognition in arena assays; see Home-cage monitoring for HomeCageScan
details: A commercial CleverSys package that automatically recognizes rodent behaviors from video in arena-based assays. The same company offers HomeCageScan for home-cage recordings, which is listed separately under home-cage monitoring.

name: Noldus DanioVision
description: Zebrafish larva activity tracking
details: A commercial Noldus system for tracking the activity of zebrafish larvae, typically in multi-well plates. It records and analyzes larval movement and is commonly used for higher-throughput screening of locomotor responses.

name: ViewPoint (ZebraLab)
description: Zebrafish and rodent behaviour tracking; see Home-cage monitoring for PhenoRack
details: A commercial ViewPoint software suite for video tracking of zebrafish and rodent behavior. The company also offers PhenoRack for home-cage work, which is listed separately under home-cage monitoring.

name: Panlab SMART
description: Video tracking for rodent behavioural tests
details: A commercial Panlab video tracking package for scoring rodent behavioral tests such as mazes and open fields. It tracks animal position from video and outputs movement and zone-based measures.

name: TSE Systems
description: Conditioning, treadmill and inhalation systems; see Home-cage monitoring for IntelliCage, PhenoMaster and InfraMot
details: A commercial vendor offering behavioral research equipment including conditioning, treadmill and inhalation systems. Its home-cage products, IntelliCage, PhenoMaster and InfraMot, are listed separately under home-cage monitoring.

name: DigiGait
description: Treadmill-based gait analysis
details: A commercial gait analysis system in which rodents walk or run on a motorized treadmill while their paws are filmed from below. It produces quantitative gait measures, allowing walking to be assessed at controlled speeds.

name: BehaviorCloud
description: Cloud platform for maze-test video tracking, manual scoring and data sharing (Conduct Science)
details: A cloud-based platform from Conduct Science for maze-test video tracking, manual behavior scoring and data sharing. Because it runs in the cloud, recordings and results can be accessed and shared without installing local analysis software.

name: TopMouseTracker
description: OpenCV tracking of mouse position and nest building in home-cage RGB-D video
details: Python library built on OpenCV that tracks a mouse in its home cage from a Kinect camera's color and depth video. It segments the animal and the nesting material frame by frame to measure location and to extract bouts of nest-building behavior automatically. It was written for a study of maternal preparatory nesting in pregnant mice.

name: Trackoscope
description: Low-cost autonomous tracking microscope for swimming microorganisms
details: A two-axis motorized microscope that follows a single swimming organism, from about 10 micrometers to 2 millimeters in size, across an area roughly the size of an A5 sheet for hours to days at high resolution. Removing the need to confine organisms under a coverslip allows long-term recording of more natural behavior, demonstrated with amoebae, ciliates and tardigrades. It is built from inexpensive, open hardware.

name: PiVR
description: Raspberry Pi platform for closed-loop tracking and virtual-reality optogenetics in freely moving animals
details: Raspberry Pi Virtual Reality tracks a freely moving animal at about 70 Hz and triggers optogenetic light stimulation from its position with under 30 ms latency, creating virtual odor or light gradients. It costs under US$500, takes a few hours to build and is extensively documented. The paper demonstrates chemotaxis and phototaxis experiments in adult flies, fly larvae and zebrafish larvae.

name: NC4Gate
description: Modular, low-cost automated gates for rodent mazes
details: An open-source gate system for building automated rodent mazes and tasks from low-cost hardware. The gates are designed to run thousands of cycles between maintenance, and up to 512 can be controlled from one computer, either interactively through a Python graphical interface or from scripts through an API. Hardware designs, software and documentation are shared openly.

name: Pirecorder
description: Python package for controlled, scheduled image and video recording on a Raspberry Pi
details: A Python package that makes the Raspberry Pi camera practical for research recordings. It helps set up the camera and its image settings consistently, and then schedule automated, repeated image or video recordings, for example across many parallel setups. It also includes tools for converting the recorded media.

name: Pi USB Cam
description: DIY Raspberry Pi USB camera for behavior video recording
details: Build guide for a low-cost video camera made from a Raspberry Pi, off-the-shelf electronics, open-source webcam firmware and 3D-printed cases. It works as a plug-and-play USB camera that common behavioral and neural recording software can use, captures wide fields of view at short distances, and keeps stable frame rates in low light and darkness. The paper provides a parts list and step-by-step build instructions.
